summary: Fire tower on a summit north of Capreol in Greater Sudbury; a May 2023 hiking account includes photos of it, reached by a steep trail.

access.note: Hiking trail from roadside parking on Portelance Road, a dirt road that may have logging traffic. The 2023 account mentions no closure or permission requirement.

visit.trail_note: About 1.5 km steep hike with a 174 m (570 ft) climb from Portelance Road; roadside parking only. The account says trees mostly block the summit view unless you climb the tower, and advises caution.

evidence.supports: summit fire tower reached north of Capreol
evidence.quote: From Capreol continue north on Regional Road 84 for 8.0 km and then turn right onto Portelance Road.

evidence.supports: the hike reaches the summit and fire tower
evidence.quote: Arrived at the summit / fire tower (12:10 PM)

evidence.supports: first fire lookout towers in Ontario in the 1920s
evidence.quote: The first fire lookout towers in Ontario appeared on the scene in the 1920s.
By 1962, there were a total of 316 steel towers in operation throughout the province

evidence.supports: towers under Department of Lands and Forests, which became MNR in 1972
evidence.quote: they came under the jurisdiction of Ontario's former Department of Lands and Forests which became the Ministry of Natural Resources in 1972.

evidence.supports: hike about 1.5 km and steep, 174 m (570 ft) climb
evidence.quote: It is a short (1.5 km) but steep (570 foot ascent) hike along a well travelled trail from the road.
There is no parking area, however there are spaces for roadside parking along Portelance Road just north of the trailhead.

evidence.supports: writer advises giving logging trucks plenty of room
evidence.quote: give the logging trucks a lot of space

evidence.supports: dirt road, logging may be in progress, caution advised
evidence.quote: The road may have active logging in progress, so caution is advised

evidence.supports: road used by Wahnapitae First Nation Reserve residents
evidence.quote: The first 5 km of the dirt road is fairly wide and well traveled by the residents of the Wahnapitae First Nation Reserve

evidence.supports: camp and cottage residents use the road
evidence.quote: the camp/cottage residents in the area
Looking up from the base of the Parkin Fire Tower

evidence.supports: summit view mostly obscured by trees; climbing needs caution
evidence.quote: The view at the summit is mostly obscured by trees unless you climb the fire tower (caution is advised).

evidence.supports: GPS-recorded height 490 m (1608 ft) for the location

notes_for_editor: Only one hiking account (Ontario High Points, posted June 2023) describes the tower in any detail. The register and the directory give location only. No build date, builder, design, staffing, fire or status history appears in the sources read. The blog's 'Height' (1608 feet / 490 meters) is the summit's elevation, not the tower's, so it is not used as height_m. The brief's coordinates agree with the register to within about 30 m; no correction. Facebook and YouTube search results were snippets only and are not cited. The blog's photo 'Future platform?' and the route notes were not used.
